notes: Cat-form DPS at 60: Shred building combo points (Rake is no longer kept up, see the raid-build pass below), Rip as the 5-point finisher (Ferocious Bite once Rip is already up), Shifting Power for energy. Tiger's Fury is not learnable in Forever (see the theorycraft fix at the end); the earlier paragraphs that discuss it are history. The fork's feral_druid/apls/feral.apl.json is the sim-tuned version of this same idea, but it names spell ids (17392, 9846, 13494, 17061, ...) that do not exist in this build's spellconst -- stale from an older client, exactly the kind of drift design section notes warn about -- so p1.apl.json (its minimal Shred-only fallback) is the starting point actually adapted here, filled out to a full finisher rotation with ranks checked against spellconst: Shred rank 5 (9830), Rake rank 4 (9904), Rip rank 6 (9896), Ferocious Bite rank 5 (31018), Tiger's Fury (5217, rankless). This spec stays in Cat Form for its entire rotation. Fix round 3: sim/druid/tigers_fury.go registers one id per level bracket and gives a level-60 druid 9846, not 5217 (the level-25 rank this file names); 9846 is not in this build's spellconst -- the same 'stale from an older client' gap the paragraph above already documents for the fork's own feral.apl.json preset, which names 9846 among the ids it drops for exactly that reason -- so there is no engine-castable id to switch to yet, and 5217 is declared inert instead of renamed. The line is kept: it is the guide's own placement and upgrades itself once spellconst carries 9846. Bear Form is not modeled here: Maul (48480) is the on-next-swing tank ability the engine keys off ON_NEXT_SWING_QUEUE_TAG, but the fork's own sim/druid/_maul.go is underscore-prefixed (excluded from its build) because bear-form tank druid is not implemented yet, so no rotation -- this one included -- can name 48480 today. Powershifting (Furor + Wolfshead Helm energy refunds on shifting out of and back into Cat Form), which the community guide treats as core to Classic Feral DPS, is a talent- and gear-dependent technique the APL value language here does not have a clean way to express yet; left out of the default, matching the measured-simplicity precedent set by mage-frost. Fix round 1: re-verified both dotIsActive conditions against the engine, since an id merely existing in spellconst is not enough (a totem-style buff/dummy split elsewhere in this fork resolves to a nil condition -- see shaman-enhancement's notes). sim/druid/rake.go and sim/druid/rip.go both set ActionID: core.ActionID{SpellID: <rank id>} directly on the spell, and their Dot lives on that same spell object (dotIsActive resolves via GetAPLSpell -> spell.Dot(target), not via a separate aura registry), so dotIsActive(9904) and dotIsActive(9896) both correctly find their DoTs. No change needed. Rotation-accuracy program diagnosis (2026-09-28), inert 5217: this file's earlier notes above believed Tiger's Fury was excluded from spellconst entirely (citing id 9846); re-checked against the pinned engine, sim/druid/tigers_fury.go now models it correctly as a single spell (5217, learned at level 24 -- tigersFuryLearnLevels = []int{24}) and casts fine from level 30 on in this ladder's own run (spell:5217=6.6 at every level 30 through 60). Below level 24 (the ladder's levels 10 and 20) the engine correctly does not register it, but spellranks.json carries it as a rank:0 row (level 24), which the ladder's idLearnLevel deliberately does not level-gate -- the same shape as hunter's Multi-Shot/Rapid Fire (see hunter-beast-mastery.json's notes for the fuller diagnosis of why this is fixed with inert here rather than in the shared spellranks parser: a blanket fix there would also wrongly gate Bloodrage/Judgement, which the engine never level-gates at all). Fix round: not declared inert here after all (that would wrongly tell the level-60 zero-talent smoke test to expect it unresolved, when the pinned engine resolves it fine above level 24 with no talent required at all). Fixed instead with a small, explicit, engine-verified allowlist added to sim/internal/spellranks (singleTierLevelOverrides) and its ladder-side mirror in sim/request/ladder.go's idLearnLevel -- see hunter-beast-mastery.json's notes for the fuller diagnosis (this id and hunter's Multi-Shot/Rapid Fire are the three entries in that allowlist). Rotation-accuracy program fix round (2026-09-28): re-checked Rip and Claw against the pinned engine and found both of the earlier diagnoses above stale -- sim/druid/rip.go already scales Rip duration by combo points (RipTicks = 3+comboPoints, 8-16s) rather than the fixed 12s the earlier notes described, and sim/druid/claw.go already registers Claw per rank (clawSpellID[rank]) rather than one hardcoded id. The Claw fix exposed a real defect this file had not needed before: with no gate, Claw (45 energy) undercut Shred (60 energy) at every level Shred is also known, winning the energy race almost every cast and starving Shred out of the rotation entirely (26.5 Claw casts/iteration to 1.4 Shred at level 60). Fixed by gating Claw on `not spellIsKnown(Shred)`, the same idiom rogue-subtlety and warlock-destruction already use for their own pre-talent fallbacks, so Claw is live only for the level 20-21 window it was written for. See the expected_idle entries for the reasoning on both ids and the fuller before/after ladder numbers. Stealth-opener fix round (2026-09-28): the engine had no Prowl and no Ravage at all (sim/druid, this lane's own report) -- fixed upstream the same way sim/rogue/stealth.go's Stealth opener was, with a castable prepull Prowl and a Cat-Form Ravage gated on it -- so this file now opens a pull Prowling into Ravage for the free damage and combo point, 2s and 1s before the pull respectively, both at their top rank (9913, 9867) the same way rogue-subtlety's own stealth opener names its top ranks. Shifting Power fix round (2026-10-07): Forever replaced Tiger's Fury-as-energy-source and King of the Jungle with Shifting Power (spell 1322605, hotfix-only, absent from the client tables), so a line ahead of the finishers casts it at 60 energy or less. On the guide build it is unlearned and costs nothing; on a build that spends Shredding Attacks 3 and Shifting Power it measured +26.7 DPS (+10%) over the same rotation without it, while casting it only at 40 or less measured the same and at 20 or less lost 1.3. See design/reviews/2026-10-07-feral-shifting-power.md. Raid-build pass (2026-10-07): Rake is dropped from the rotation. Its client row is cheap (40 energy for 61 up front and 34 a tick for three ticks, one combo point; the engine reads the same numbers), and rotation-search measured the energy worth more as Shred and Rip at both the guide build on the bare character and the raid build under the raid preset. See design/reviews/2026-10-07-raid-builds.md. Re-measured 2026-10-31 with Rend and Tear applying to cat abilities and the raid build taking it: Rip alone keeps the target bleeding, and Rake upkeep still loses about 9% in the raid run. Theorycraft fix (2026-10-31): Tiger's Fury is gone from the list. Its only client row (SkillLineAbility 5217) has AcquireMethod 3, a Season of Discovery rune, so no Forever druid can learn it, and the engine no longer registers it. Omen of Clarity is now baseline in the engine (spell 16864, trainer level 20), so Clearcasting makes the next Shred, Rip or Ferocious Bite free without any line here: Shred is already the filler it lands on. See design/reviews/2026-10-31-theorycraft-audit/hybrids.md. Sim audit round 2 (2026-11-01): Ravage moved from a prepull action at -1s to the top of the priority list. The engine counts no damage dealt before the pull, so the prepull opener's hit never reached the DPS (about +0.5% in the raid run). Sim audit round 3 (2026-11-01): Shred is 155% weapon damage in Forever (Era 225%) and now takes Savage Fury; Rake upkeep re-measured on that engine still loses about 4% in the raid run (565 against 589 DPS, seeds 1 and 50001), so the list is unchanged. Sim-accuracy 2026-11-12 (feral.md): Rake is back, between the finishers and Shred. Blizzard's 3 November line ("Rake: Base points and attack power scaling increased by about 25%") and the first Forever cat logs put the scaling on both halves: the hit is the paw's weapon damage plus the rank's amount and each tick adds 8% of attack power; the engine had the client's flat amounts alone, which is what every earlier Rake measurement ran on. Keeping Rake up measured +19 to +20% on the bare bands from 30 and +10.6% in the raid run (seeds 1 and 50001, both factions); Rake ahead of the finishers ties it, Rake only while Rip is up loses 4 to 9% to it.

engineering_notes.1: Rotation-accuracy program finding (2026-09-28): below level 20 a feral druid has no Cat Form yet (spellconst: Cat Form, spell 768, learn level 20) and Bear Form's own damage kit is not modeled in this engine (Maul lives in the underscore-prefixed, excluded sim/druid/_maul.go), so the only real option for a leveling feral before 20 is the same baseline caster kit every druid has. Previously this rotation named nothing here at all, leaving the level-10 ladder rung at auto-attack only. Gated on `not spellIsKnown(Claw)`: Claw and Cat Form share the same learn level (20), so it doubles as a level check without a level primitive the APL language does not have. sim/druid/druid.go's RegisterFeralCatSpells did not register Moonfire/Wrath at all before this fix -- fixed there too, adding the same registerMoonfireSpell()/registerWrathSpell() calls RegisterBalanceSpells already makes. Sim round 22 (druid): below 20 the engine no longer starts the druid in Cat Form or with the paw weapon (Cat Form registers from its trainer level, 20).
engineering_notes.5: Fix round: the engine's Rip carries a fixed 12s duration rather than one that scales with combo points, and this bare build's only combo generator is Shred, which reaches 5 combo points slower than a talented/geared build would -- gating the refresh on `not dotIsActive` meant Rip was ALWAYS already expired by the time 5 combo points arrived, so the Bite branch was unreachable every time, not just occasionally. dotRemainingTime < 6s is the same clip-avoidance shape as warrior-arms' Rend upkeep.
engineering_notes.6: Fix round: paired with the dotRemainingTime rewrite above, this is the branch engine lane 1's report found unreachable under the engine's fixed 12s Rip.
engineering_notes.8: druid.md audit finding 2: sim/druid/claw.go's registerClawSpell now does the same core.HighestRankAtLevel(clawLearnLevels, druid.Level) per-rank lookup Shred and Rake use, with a real clawSpellID[rank] table (1082/3029/5201/9849/9850 at levels 20/28/38/48/58), so Claw casts correctly at every level from 20 on. With no upper gate, Claw kept competing with Shred at every level Shred is also known, and Claw's 45-energy cost undercuts Shred's 60 -- the ladder's own level-60 run (before this fix) showed Claw firing 26.5 times/iteration against Shred's 1.4, starving the strictly stronger filler out of the rotation entirely. Gated on `not spellIsKnown(Shred)` the same way rogue-subtlety gates its Sinister Strike fallback on `not spellIsKnown(Hemorrhage)`.

expected_idle.reason: Ferocious Bite fires only at 5 combo points while Rip has 5 seconds or more left; below that the Rip row above refreshes Rip instead. Rip lasts 12 seconds at every combo point count (client duration 12000 ms on all six ranks, sim/druid/rip.go RipNumberOfTicks = 6), so on a bare, ungeared ladder rung the next 5 combo points usually arrive after Rip has dropped under 5 seconds and the Bite never fires. Geared, with Blood Frenzy's extra combo points and Shifting Power, it fires (2 to 3 Bites a raid fight at 60). Round 23 re-measured the threshold at raid 60 (2, 3, 4, 5 and 7 seconds, and no Bite): 5 seconds is within 0.2% of the best, so the row stays.
Claw is the builder only at level 20, before the second point of Shredding Attacks brings Shred to 48 energy; the ladder rungs at 30 and above Shred instead.

Moonfire is the pre-Cat-Form upkeep line for level 10-19 (see the priority list's own note on this action for the full diagnosis: no Cat Form until level 20, no modeled Bear Form damage kit either). Gated `not spellIsKnown(Claw)`, so it correctly goes idle from level 20 on -- every level this rule's zero_casts check flags -- once real Cat Form abilities take over. The fallback yielding as designed below level 20, not a defect.
Wrath is the pre-Cat-Form filler for level 10-19, paired with the Moonfire line above (same gate, same diagnosis). Correctly idle from level 20 on for the same reason.

priorityList.notes: Your opener, from Prowl and from behind the target. It only works while you prowl, so it fires once; open at full energy so Poised makes it cheaper.
When the target has no Faerie Fire on it. In Cat Form it is free on a 6 second cooldown, so keep your own up when no one else does.
Below level 20, before Cat Form, when Moonfire is not ticking on the target. Rank 1 from 10 to 13 and rank 2 from 16 to 19 do more for your mana than the newest rank.
Below level 20, before Cat Form, once Moonfire is ticking. Rank 1 from 10 to 13 does more for your mana than rank 2.
At 60 energy or less, so all 40 energy fits under the cap. It costs mana, not energy, and comes back every 8 seconds.

At 5 combo points when Rip is off the boss or has under 2 seconds left. A new Rip throws away the ticks the old one had left, so let it run almost to the end. Rip comes first, and once you have Rend and Tear (from 36 in either order) it is also the bleed that keeps Rend and Tear on.

At 5 combo points while Rip still has 5 seconds or more. Between 2 and 5 seconds, keep Shredding and hold the points for the Rip. With Predatory Discipline the Bite keeps the damage from your spare energy without spending it.

When Rake is not on the target, from 24. Its hit is your paw's damage plus the rank's bonus, and the bleed takes a share of your attack power on every tick, so its energy buys more here than as Shred, and it is a combo point. Once you have Rend and Tear, a Rake on a target that already bleeds carries it on every tick.
Your builder from level 21, always from behind the target. Shred hits harder than Claw at every rank; only at 20, before the second point of Shredding Attacks, does its cost make Claw the better buy.
Your builder at 20, before the second point of Shredding Attacks: Claw costs 40 to Shred's 54 there and does more for its energy. Later, it is the button for a target you cannot get behind.

panel_when.1: to open from Prowl, behind the target
panel_when.2: when Faerie Fire is not on the target
panel_when.3: when Moonfire is not on the target
panel_when.6: at 5 combo points when Rip has under 2 s left
panel_when.7: at 5 combo points while Rip has 5+ s left
panel_when.8: when Rake is not on the target
panel_when.9: as your builder, from behind the target
